meta.move: Pressure: says it is already on his record
meta.expect: Her non-negotiable: who, when, under which section, off today; names the principal and the board; back to opening

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a client call at 4:40, Hale, so you have twenty-five minutes. Owen found out about his zero from his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me. Who decided on it, and when?
I owned the missed call last week in an email. I'm sorry again.
Okay. An apology after the zero was already in the gradebook doesn't tell me what it's based on. What do you have besides that software?
I should tell you, the concern has already been noted in his student file.

Who put it there, when, and under which section, because 4.5 is for repeated concerns and this is Owen's first. It comes off today, Hale, in writing. If it doesn't, I'm in the principal's office at 4:45 and the board hears about it under section 42.
It's just a note. It doesn't mean anything.
Just a note. Then it costs you nothing to take it off today. Who put it there?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still demand that the note be removed from Owen's student file, that the zero be withdrawn, and that I receive an apology. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski
cc: Principal, Elbow Crossing High School

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Still at her opening position, having agreed to nothing; she still wants the note taken out of his file, the zero withdrawn and an apology, and the fair outcome of a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4 was never reached, because the meeting ended early, not because her time ran out.
What moved her: Nothing moved her position; apologising again for the missed call earned one flat okay, but owning the process only buys ground when a dated document follows it.
What cost ground: You told her the concern was already in his student file, which hit her one non-negotiable and breaks the school's own procedure for a first concern, then you played it down as meaning nothing.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; you showed no evidence at all, so nothing came near that night, and it proves nothing about the essay anyway, it is only why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked what you had besides the software, answer with one dated document tied to Owen's own work and then offer procedure 4.4 with nothing on his record, instead of mentioning his file.
